text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thirteen Israelis killed and 170 wounded in two horrific explosions that took place at the biggest market in west Jerusalem. President Hosni Mubarak reaffirms Egypt's refusal of terrorist acts in his telephone conversations with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, President Ezer Weizman and Labour leader Ehud Barak. Mubarak sends condolence messages to Netanyahu and Weizman.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says the Israel attack supports Mubarak's warnings that the situation is dangerous.
- Cabinet decides after meeting: the situation is settled between tenant farmers and land owners.
- Proof of the confidence investors have in the Egyptian economy: France picks Cairo as the place to hold an international meeting for its businessmen.
- Yemeni president says Mubarak is playing a leading role in clearing the Arab atmosphere and setting up a common market.
- Cabinet meeting headed by Prime Minister Ganzouri decides to update the irrigation system and cancel the blockage of some of the flow of the Nile behind the Aswan Dam in winter.
- IMF denies it is putting any pressure on Egypt to appreciate the value of pound.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali says Egypt is free from any agricultural products that have been genetically engineered.
- Egypt to give back the third tranche of taxes paid by expatriates.
